To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the majority of the Chinese students are not passive learners, (2) they are not only active in their learning but also willing to seek help when necessary, (3) the majority of them are not rote learners, and (4) the majority of Chinese teachers are not authoritarian and do not use the lecture method exclusively.
(1) Chinese students' approaches to studying and their learning strategies are similar to those of their counterparts in other countries.
the students' selfefficacy, their perceptions of the learning environment and their learning strategies are important determinants of their learning outcomes in mathematics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the Chinese learners, their teachers and the teaching learning environment that is unique to the Chinese context.
how the Chinese learners learn in their home country and how they learn in the Western world.
how students learn and how teachers teach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Chinese learners are paradoxical.
the notion of the Chinese learner is a contested one, and the Chinese learners are a complex and multifaceted group.
the Chinese learner is an evolving notion that is not static.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the Chinese learner is not a stereotype but a concept that is evolving in a dynamic and interactive manner.
the Chinese learners and teachers have a unique way of approaching learning that is different from Western learners.

we are interested in understanding and promoting the development of the Chinese learners' academic achievement, and in particular the development of Chinese learners' learning strategies, learning motivation and learning attitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chinese learners are not a homogeneous group. They have their own unique characteristics, and they also have their own problems.
the Chinese learners are not a stereotype, but an emerging concept that needs to be understood within a changing educational context.
the Chinese learner is a complex concept that cannot be reduced to a single dimension, and that the Chinese learner discourse is an ongoing discourse that is constantly evolving.
